title: Bibenzyl analogue DS-1 inhibits MDM2-mediated p53 degradation and sensitizes apoptosis in lung cancer cells.
authors: Putri, Hardyanti Eka; Nutho, Bodee; Rungrotmongkol, Thanyada; Sritularak, Boonchoo; Vinayanuwattikun, Chanida; Chanvorachote, Pithi
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子DS-1抑制MDM2介导的p53降解并增敏肺癌细胞凋亡，虽含MDM2-p53蛋白互作与分子对接，但对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法仅简单对接，与TF-DNA课题关联弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer is a leading fatal malignancy due to the high incidence of treatment failure. Dysfunction of the tumor suppressor p53 contributes to cancer initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. Targeting MDM2, a negative regulator of p53, has recently attracted interest in cancer drug research as it may restore tumor suppressive function. PURPOSE: The present study aimed to investigate the effect of 3,4-dihydroxy-5,4'-dimethoxybibenzyl (DS-1) on targeting MDM2 and restoring p53 function in lung cancer cells. METHODS: The efficacy of DS-1 alone or in combination with cisplatin in lung cancer cells was determined by MTT, nuclear staining, and annexin V/PI assay. The expression of apoptosis-related proteins was determined by western blot analysis. To evaluate the role of DS-1 on the stabilization and degradation of p53, cycloheximide chasing assay and immunoprecipitation were conducted, and the active form of p53 was investigated by immunofluorescent staining assay. To confirm and demonstrate the site interaction between DS-1 and the MDM2 protein, in silico computational analysis was performed. RESULTS: DS-1 exhibited a cytotoxic effect and sensitized lung cancer cells to cisplatin-induced apoptosis. DS-1 caused a significant increase in the cellular level of p53 protein, while the active form of p53 (phosphorylation at Ser15) was unaltered. DS-1 treatment in combination with cisplatin could enhance activated p-p53 (Ser15) and p53 downstream signaling (Bax, Bcl-2, and Akt), leading to a higher level of apoptosis. Immunoprecipitation analysis revealed that DS-1 decreased the p53-ubiquitin complex, a prerequisite step in p53 proteasomal degradation. Molecular docking simulation further evidenced that DS-1 interacts with MDM2 within the p53-binding domain by carbon-hydrogen bond interaction at Lys27, pi-alkyl interactions at Ile37 and Leu30, and van der Waals interactions at Ile75, Val51, Val69, Phe67, Met38, Tyr43, Gly34, and Phe31. Treatment by DS-1 and cisplatin in patient-derivated primary lung cancer cells showed consistent effects by increasing cisplatin sensitivity. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide evidence that DS-1 is an MDM2 inhibitor and its underlying mechanism involves MDM2 binding and p53 induction, which may benefit the development of this compound for lung cancer treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：肺癌是一种主要的致命恶性肿瘤，因为治疗失败的发生率很高。肿瘤抑制因子p53的功能障碍有助于癌症的发生、进展和治疗耐药性。靶向MDM2（p53的负调控因子）近来在癌症药物研究中引起关注，因为它可能恢复肿瘤抑制功能。目的：本研究旨在探讨3,4-二羟基-5,4'-二甲氧基联苄（DS-1）在肺癌细胞中靶向MDM2并恢复p53功能的效果。方法：通过MTT、核染色和annexin V/PI实验测定DS-1单独或与顺铂联合在肺癌细胞中的疗效。通过western blot分析凋亡相关蛋白的表达。为评估DS-1对p53稳定性和降解的作用，进行了环己酰亚胺追踪实验和免疫沉淀，并通过免疫荧光染色实验研究p53的活性形式。为确认和展示DS-1与MDM2蛋白之间的位点相互作用，进行了计算机模拟分析。结果：DS-1表现出细胞毒性效应，并使肺癌细胞对顺铂诱导的凋亡敏感。DS-1显著增加p53蛋白的细胞水平，而p53的活性形式（Ser15磷酸化）未改变。DS-1与顺铂联合处理可增强活化的p-p53（Ser15）和p53下游信号传导（Bax、Bcl-2和Akt），导致更高水平的凋亡。免疫沉淀分析显示，DS-1减少了p53-泛素复合物，这是p53蛋白酶体降解的先决步骤。分子对接模拟进一步证明，DS-1通过Lys27处的碳氢键相互作用、Ile37和Leu30处的pi-烷基相互作用，以及Ile75、Val51、Val69、Phe67、Met38、Tyr43、Gly34和Phe31处的范德华相互作用，与MDM2在p53结合域内相互作用。在患者来源的原代肺癌细胞中，DS-1和顺铂处理显示出通过增加顺铂敏感性的一致效果。结论：我们的发现提供了证据，表明DS-1是一种MDM2抑制剂，其潜在机制涉及MDM2结合和p53诱导，这可能有助于该化合物在肺癌治疗中的开发。
